Also, when did these issues first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-year-old male. The patient has been increasingly disruptive in class according to his teacher. He often refuses to participate in directed activities with responses such as 'You're not the boss of me' or 'You can't make me.' He is reluctant to participate in gym class, though he engages actively in similar physical activities during recess. You mentioned the mother's description was cut off; could you finish that thought and tell me if there are any specific triggers for his defiance, such as transitions between activities or demanding tasks? Additionally, has he ever been diagnosed with ADHD or autism spectrum disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Lives with mother, father, and a younger sister. Performs well academically when he chooses to engage. No known substance use in the family.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any symptoms of depression or anxiety. No history of bullying or feeling unsafe at school or home. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an unusual diagnosis for these behavioral symptoms; a UTI typically presents with pain or frequency, not defiance. Could you clarify exactly what the doctor said, and does the patient have any urinary symptoms like urgency or bedwetting? Additionally, do his disruptive outbursts improve when he is physically active or focused on a favorite topic?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS. No urinary symptoms such as urgency, dysuria, frequency, or bedwetting reported. Disruptive outbursts do not improve with physical activity or focus on favorite topics in a manner consistent with hyperactivity or anxiety relief. Urinalysis and Abdominal Ultrasound results are within normal limits, showing no evidence of infection or anatomical abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)

The normal urinary tests rule out a medical cause, and the pattern of defiance without mood symptoms points toward a behavioral disorder. Does his defiance specifically target authority figures (parents, teachers) while he remains respectful to peers, and do these behaviors interfere significantly with his relationships or daily routine?
